prediction.likelyOutcome: U.S. Bank is well-positioned to prevail on both the foreclosure and in personam money judgment claims given the documented loan, default, and forbearance history, and the borrower's failure to object to the combined pleading forecloses a likely procedural attack; expect a judgment at or very near the pled $46,290,900.25 figure plus additional accrued interest, fees and costs proven at or after trial. The chief residual risk is the unspecified nature of the borrower's trial defenses, which the two years of contested liability litigation shows are real but which cannot be quantified from this record.

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court held Penn Realty breached the loan agreement and entered an in personam money judgment for U.S. Bank of $51,392,086.96 (no judgment in mortgage foreclosure was entered); the Third Circuit affirmed that judgment in a separate unpublished opinion (No. 23-2185, Sept. 25, 2024). In this precedential appeal the Third Circuit upheld the subsequent execution sale of the apartment building under Fed. R. Civ. P. 69(a) and affirmed the denial of the borrower's motion to quash.
